newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa puts stamp on corporate merger.
newsitem.headline: Axa puts stamp on corporate merger.

text.p: French insurer Axa SA put its stamp on Wednesday on the new corporate entity to be created by its megamerger with rival UAP, announcing an executive lineup dominated by Axa nominees.

In a clear signal of which company would call the shots, Axa and UAP also said the new group would use the name Axa worldwide as its brand name. In a nod to UAP, the name of the holding company resulting from the merger will be Axa-UAP.

"Given the increasingly global nature of business and markets, it is essential that the new group ultimately use a single brand name around the world. This single brand name will be Axa," Axa and UAP said.

After Axa denied press reports it would dominate the new administration, it emerged that 10 of the 16 members of the executive committee responsible for overseeing the group's strategic and financial operations would be from Axa.
The committee's membership was announced in a statement after the closure of Axa's paper offer for UAP -- Union des Assurances de Paris -- valued at 40 billion francs ($7.66 billion).
The two companies said the results of the exchange offer proposed by Axa to UAP shareholders would be known on January 13 "but it is widely acknowledged to have been very successful".
Axa insisted when the deal was announced last month it represented "a friendly operation between equals".
Insurance analysts said all along they had little doubt highly profitable Axa would hold sway over the larger, formerly state-owned UAP, which only recently returned to profit.

"We really don't care about which company the people came from. What mattered to us was competence...who was best for the job," said an Axa spokeswoman. The choice, she said, was also tilted toward those with international experience.
Axa shares jumped 1.54 percent to 309.50 francs on investor relief that there would be no power struggle after newspapers had reported tense jockeying for the top spots.
"It's good news for investors that Axa's going to be running the show. It has a reputation for being able to take over companies and turn them around," said one Paris analyst.
The daily Le Monde reported UAP chairman Jacques Friedmann wanted UAP and Axa to be represented equally while Axa chairman Claude Bebear wanted to "impose the Axa stamp at all levels".
Under the new two-tier management structure, UAP chairman Jacques Friedmann is to be chairman of the supervisory board.
But analysts said the real power would be wielded by Bebear who becomes chairman of the executive board of the holding, making him effectively chief executive officer.
The executive committee will meet every six weeks while the supervisory commitee, whose makeup will be announced soon, will discuss long-term strategy and meet three times a year.
Those on the panel include Dominique Bazy, head of UAP France, seen as one of its stars and and Geoff Tomlinson, managing head of Axa's recent buy National Mutual in Australia.
The merger will create the world's second largest insurer, with annual premium income of more than 300 billion francs.

Boosters say it is another of the bold acquisitions that have turned Axa from a sleepy mutual into a global powerhouse in two decades. But others say it may have underestimated hurdles in absorbing UAP, France's largest insurer, which has a stodgy reputation and whose French network overlaps its own.

In wake of the merger, Axa said on Wednesday it was rowing back from its forecast of achieving a return on equity of 15 percent by the year 2000, saying the new group hoped to achieve that goal as soon as possible after that date.

"Before the merger, we (Axa) were saying we hoped to attain 15 percent return on equity in the year 2000. Now we are saying as soon as possible (for the new merged group) after this date but we are not saying when yet," said a spokeswoman. ($1=5.224 French Franc)
